name: Talos
long_description: At Talos, we are building better, more modern predictive maintenance for the power industry with a focus on large transformers. Our devices continuously monitor critical power equipment and detect problems early on using anomaly-detection models. For each fault, we provide detailed analyses of the problem, exactly where and why it happened, as well as next steps teams should take.

launches.title: Talos: Early-warning system for power grid infrastructure
launches.tagline: Detect faults before they become catastrophic failures.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Talos is building an early-warning platform that uses retrofittable sensors and machine learning to detect issues on critical power equipment before they cause multi-million dollar failures. 

**Video:** <https://youtu.be/E43rheBR8FI>  

**Problem**

America’s power grid is struggling:

* Power outages cost Americans over $125 billion just last year, and power failures have more than doubled since 2024.
* 75% of today’s power comes from machines operating past their intended lifespan. 
* With the rise of AI and rapid scaling of compute, demand for power has doubled in the past five years.

Despite this, most utilities still run their equipment till failure and rely on outdated monitoring systems, reacting to problems as they happen. 

**Our solution**

Talos deploys non-invasive, retrofittable sensors on power equipment and continuously monitors vibration, magnetic flux, temperature, and humidity. We learn what normal and faulty behavior looks like for your machine, allowing us to detect small issues before they become catastrophic failures.

With sensors deployed across 40+ assets, Talos is partnering with national laboratories, utilities and plant owners to monitor transformers, turbines, pumps, poles, and generators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123793&key=user_uploads/3099707/8bebc26c-1b9d-43b7-9967-6f858a48ddeb)

**Our Asks:** 

* Know any grid operators or anyone working with large-scale power equipment such as transformers, turbines, pumps, or generators? Please share this post. We’d love an introduction. 
* If this sounds interesting or if you are also in the power and energy space, we would love to connect! Reach out to us at [founders@talos-us.com](mailto:founders@talos-us.com).

Learn more at [talos-us.com](http://talos-us.com). 

\- Amitav, Himani, and Kevin
